claim_map.quantifiers: Every finite simple undirected loopless G, every fixed strictly positive vertex-rate vector, every fixed positive integer initial edge-count vector; every exponent α>4/3; with probability one (V,E∞) is a forest. Isolated vertices are harmless.
claim_map.mechanism: Exclude even cycles at all α>1 and odd cycles by weighted Hessian estimate, then apply imported finite convergence/support and integer-start tail transfer.

claim_map.quantifiers: For each1<α<4/3, the equal-rate triangle with unit initial counts retains all three edges with positive probability. Therefore no lower strict universal threshold works. No claim atα=4/3.
claim_map.mechanism: Known uniform triangle equilibrium: Jacobian eigenvalues−1 and3α/4−1 twice; known positive attainment for strictly stable equilibria.

claim_map.quantifiers: Same finite/simple/loopless/integer model, with equal positive firing rates; every α≥17/4; with probability one every surviving component is a tree of diameter≤3. A star is allowed; no bound on number of leaves.
claim_map.mechanism: Least positive edge≥1; internal edge≤3/2 contradicts a necessary diagonal stability inequality, by five closed rational intervals and analytic tail; heavier internal edges form a matching.

claim_map.quantifiers: Every valid equilibrium whose positive support contains an even cycle is linearly unstable forα>1. For an odd support cycle lengthm, instability holds forα>sec²(π/(2m)). Arbitrary positive rates, unequal equilibrium weights, chords and attachments allowed.

limitations: Finite graphs only. No theorem for infinite WARM graphs, no claim that all infinite-graph surviving components are finite, and no conditioning shortcut from an infinite component to a finite process.
Forest conclusion permits unequal positive rates; whisker conclusion requires equal rates. Unequal-rate long-path stable examples are known.
Initial counts are fixed positive integers. Zero counts, positive noninteger offsets, loops and multigraph extensions are not asserted.
α=4/3 is excluded from the forest theorem and its attainment argument. The equal-rate whisker threshold17/4 is sufficient and inclusive, not claimed optimal.

Survival means infinitely many reinforcements E∞; its identification with positive limiting linear growth uses the imported support theorem. This is not merely a statement about a deterministic support.
Almost sure universal structural conclusions differ from the positive-probability unit-triangle obstruction. No realization probabilities, convergence rates or finite observation times are supplied.
Whisker means tree of diameter at most3, including arbitrarily large stars; no vertex-count bound or unique survivor graph follows.
No claim about empirically observed neural networks or biological validity follows from the stochastic graph model.
The paper is an AI-assisted unrefereed preprint. No external human peer review, journal acceptance, proof-assistant certification or exhaustive novelty/priority claim is established.
